concept.name: Senkou Span B
concept.definition: The slower cloud boundary: the midpoint of the 52-period high-low range, plotted 26 periods ahead, forming the long-term equilibrium edge of the Kumo.
concept.intuition: The slowest Ichimoku line, it moves rarely and marks durable long-term balance; flat, thick sections of cloud built on Span B are watched as major support or resistance.
concept.mechanics: Senkou Span B = (max(High,52) + min(Low,52))/2, shifted 26 bars forward. Its relation to Senkou Span A sets the cloud color, and a price break through a Span-B-defined cloud edge signals a trend change.
concept.formula: Senkou Span B = (max(High, 52) + min(Low, 52)) / 2, plotted 26 periods into the future.
concept.failure_modes: Extreme inertia: it can sit far from price for months, making cloud-break signals late; like all Ichimoku lines it is descriptive, not predictive.
concept.misconceptions: A thick cloud is often called 'strong support/resistance', but that is a practitioner heuristic, not a tested law.
concept.example: With a 52-bar high of 112 and low of 90, Senkou Span B = 101, plotted 26 bars ahead.
